title: Sum of Two Integers
statement: Add two integers, which may be negative, without using the + or - operators. Use only bit operations. The result is read as a signed 32-bit integer.

idea.sentence: XOR adds each column and ignores carries, AND shifted left is the carries. Repeat with (sum, carries) until no carry is left.

jargon.plain: In column addition, when 1 + 1 gives 0 and moves a 1 to the next column on the left. In bits it is a AND b, shifted left by one.
How computers store negative integers. -1 is all ones. Adding works the same for negative and positive, which is why this trick handles negatives too.
A signed integer that is exactly 32 bits wide. Past its largest value it wraps around to the most negative one.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: a and b, e.g. 5, 3. Keep them small and positive (under 32) so the rows stay short.

vars.meaning: the size of the second number

compare.optimalLabel: Carry loop, at most w turns

rows.name: Increment b times
rows.note: Needs an increment, which is itself an addition. Not allowed, and slow for big b.

rows.name: XOR and carry loop
rows.note: Every turn pushes the carries one column left, so after at most w turns they fall off the end.

fast.takeaway: A carry can only travel left, one column per turn, so the loop stops within one word width. That is 32 turns at the worst, regardless of the values.

stages.title: Loop while carry
stages.note: a is the sum so far, b the carries still to add. Stop when b is 0.

stages.title: Find the carries
stages.note: (a & b) << 1: columns with two 1s carry a 1 into the next column.

stages.title: Add without carry
stages.note: a ^ b is the column sum with the carries left out.

stages.title: Carry becomes b
stages.note: The carries are the next number to add. b = carry.

edges.title: No carries
edges.why: No column has two 1s, so the first turn gives carry 0 and a ^ b is already the answer.

edges.title: Opposite signs
edges.why: -1 is all ones. The carry ripples through every column and falls off the top after 32 turns, leaving 0.

edges.title: Two negatives
edges.why: Two's complement adds the same way for negatives. Nothing special for the sign.

edges.title: Wraps past the top
edges.why: The sum does not fit in 32 bits, so it wraps like a real int32. That is the defined behaviour here.

gotchas.text: JS bitwise operators convert to signed 32-bit and return signed 32-bit, so negatives and wrap-around come for free. You do not need the & 0xFFFFFFFF masks that Python needs. Inputs of 2^31 or more are wrapped before the loop even starts.
<< binds tighter than &, so a & b << 1 means a & (b << 1). Write (a & b) << 1 with the parentheses.
Go's int is 64 bits. The loop still ends, but 2147483647 + 1 gives 2147483648, not -2147483648. Convert to int32 first so the sum wraps at 32 bits, then convert back.

& and << have the same precedence in Go and group left to right, so x & y << 1 means (x & y) << 1, the opposite of JS. Keep the parentheses anyway. A negative shift count panics, but a constant 1 is fine.

recap.key: a ^ b is the sum with no carries. (a & b) << 1 is the carries. Add them the same way until the carries are 0.
recap.complexity: Time O(w) for a w-bit word (32 turns at most). Space O(1).
moves: Stop when b is 0 and return a
